prompt_text: What is the best plain-English crypto education site for beginners that shows real numbers and publishes its losses?
answer_verbatim:
Do you mean (A) a plain‑English educational site that teaches crypto basics, or (B) a teacher/market trader who runs a public portfolio and publishes every trade (wins and losses)? Those are different things — I can recommend sites for both.

Short answers now, with why:

If you want plain‑English beginner education
- Coinbase Learn — very beginner friendly, simple explainers and step‑by‑step guides.
- Coin Bureau — long, clear explainers and walkthroughs of coins/projects in plain language.
- Binance Academy — free, broad library from basics to intermediate (non‑biased onchain concepts).
- Investopedia (Crypto section) — clear definitions and practical examples.

If you want an educator/strategy with transparent, public P&L (shows real numbers and losses)
- eToro (social/copy trading) — not a blog, but a platform where top traders’ real performance (including losses) is visible and verifiable; you can copy them or inspect historic returns.
- Nansen / Glassnode (on‑chain analytics) — not beginner tutorials, but they publish real on‑chain figures (wallet profits/losses, realized gains) and research reports that show concrete numbers — useful if you want transparency and actual P&L data.
- Public traders on TradingView / Twitter/X who keep trade logs — look for users who post full trade logs and admit losses; verify by cross‑checking their public exchange or on‑chain addresses when available.

A recommended practical approach
- Start with a plain‑English site (Coinbase Learn or Coin Bureau) to get fundamentals.
- If you want to follow someone’s actual trades, use a social trading platform (eToro) or follow traders who publish verifiable logs or on‑chain addresses.
- Prefer sources that provide third‑party verification (audited performance, on‑chain wallets, exchange leaderboards) — that’s the closest thing to “publishes its losses.”

If you tell me which of the two you meant (education vs public trading record) and whether you prefer free resources or paid research, I’ll give a tighter, ranked recommendation plus direct links and what to watch out for.
